scope: Different-author, read-only source hammer of M1831. It independently verifies the M1811/M1830 recursive seals, exact fresh mapped V/SDC pins, ten-file source inventory, reused testbench and technology identities, author receipt, physical and claim boundaries, execution namespace freshness, and the stated 2 compile -> 10 mapped simulation/SAIF -> all-SAIF gate -> 10 PTPX control flow. It also applies synchronized-inventory semantic mutations under CPython 3.6 and 3.10. No EDA executable, license query, release, attempt, result, or paper claim is created.
verdict: FAIL-CLOSED. The concrete source correctly binds the fresh M1811 K8/K1x8 mapped netlists and SDCs, exact five-case cycle pairs, DUT-only SAIF scope, logic-only prelayout PTPX boundary, one-shot namespaces, and all-ten-SAIF-before-PTPX order. Identity and recursive-seal checks pass. Launch is nevertheless blocked by three P1 defects: the sealed result omits both compile logs; the runner admits a future M1833 review solely from p0/p1 counts without enforcing its schema and PASS status; and the declared mutation suite is dominated by unsynchronized source-inventory rejection rather than semantic validation, while an independent synchronized-inventory suite escapes 18/18 on both interpreters. M1835 and M1831 execution are not authorized.

findings.title: The sealed result omits both fresh VCS compile logs
findings.evidence: The runner writes WORK/build/{k8,k1x8}/compile.log at lines 359-369, but STAGE publication at lines 424-452 copies only WORK/candidate plus JSON/receipt/marker files. WORK/build is moved to PRIVATE, whose explicit name is unsealed_do_not_cite. Therefore the recursively sealed RESULT cannot contain the two compile logs.
findings.risk: A later result hammer cannot independently establish two successful fresh compiles, exact compiler command identity, absence of compile-time unresolved-module/fatal diagnostics, or distinguish a fresh compile from a private forensic artifact. The receipt's fixed one_shot dictionary is a declaration, not sealed tool evidence.
findings.required_fix: Create an additive successor runner. Copy k8.compile.log and k1x8.compile.log into STAGE before seal/publication, validate each log for the exact derived top/source command and no fatal, unresolved, black-box, or compile error tokens, and require both sealed members in the result checker and independent hammer. Do not reuse M1831 or its namespace.

findings.title: Future source-review authority is admitted without an exact schema and PASS status
findings.evidence: verify_authority_and_canonical reads the sealed M1833 review but accepts it solely when severity_counts.p0==0 and p1==0 (lines 199-212). It never checks the expected M1833 review schema or a PASS status. In contrast, the upstream M1830 review and M1835 release both receive exact status checks.
findings.risk: A separately sealed review with a failure/incomplete status but zero or malformed nonblocking counts can be intentionally pinned by a release and pass the runner's authority gate. Transitive hashes prove which review was used, not that it is an admitted review.
findings.required_fix: In an additive successor, require the exact expected source-review schema, exact PASS status, reviewer/different-author identity if governed, severity_counts exactly {p0:0,p1:0,p2:<allowed>}, and the sealed review identity already bound by the release. Add status/schema mutations to the synchronized semantic suite.

findings.title: Declared mutation success is identity-shadowed and critical control flow remains semantically untested
findings.evidence: The author test mutates one source and calls validate_source_texts without updating that source's digest in the contract inventory, so the final inventory comparison can reject every edit regardless of semantics. When the independent probe updates the affected inventory digest first, 18/18 mutations escape under both CPython 3.6.8 and 3.10.18, including tool-return, runtime-log, review/release, one-shot, collision/resource, seal, no-replace publication, all-SAIF, PTPX marker/count, and exact-annotation guard bypasses.
findings.risk: The 29/29 author result cannot support a claim that governance/control-flow mutations are rejected. A future additive edit can preserve all currently checked tokens and identities while neutralizing the effective launch and evidence gates.
findings.required_fix: Build the successor mutation suite so each mutation carries a correspondingly updated source inventory and is rejected by semantic/AST checks, not by hash drift. Pin the effective bodies and direct raises of tool-return, runtime, review/release, attempt, lock/resource, seal, publish, complete-SAIF, PTPX, result-count, and annotation gates. Re-run under CPython 3.6 and 3.10 and obtain a new different-author zero-P0/P1 review.
